inputs.doc: E-038 READ-OUT LADDER, RE-RUN of #392 with the FIXED probe_head.py. #392's probe_kfold landed - rapid r 0.660 [0.593, 0.722] against a wind-only ridge bar of 0.670 [0.601, 0.733], i.e. two raw wind features still beat 64 mean-pooled learned ones - but BOTH ml/probe_head.py invocations were OOM-KILLED (15:00:48 and 15:26:06), and because both steps are best-effort the run went GREEN; the only honest trace was the archive step's 'not present: probe_head.json, probe_head_raw3x3.json'. Cause: an 82.8 GB TRANSIENT inside np.nan_to_num(Xa, copy=False). copy=False never copies the VALUES, but the masked-copyto form builds isnan + isposinf + isneginf, and isposinf/isneginf each build isinf and signbit underneath, so five full-size bools are live at once (measured 5.00x one bool) - 132.5 GB peak on a 126 GB box. FIXED in f2ee8b8: probe_head gets the LazyPixels treatment the #388 fix gave probe_kfold/probe_sequence/dip_check and missed here; on a 1/59-scale fixture VmHWM went 2.132 -> 0.642 GiB (3.3x). THIS RUN EXISTS TO PRODUCE ONE THING: the UNPOOLED head number - cross-attention over the ~67 raw section pixel embeddings - and its MATCHED raw-3x3 end-to-end control. That pair is the decisive test of whether E-038's headline is READ-OUT-LIMITED (the ridge on Z.mean(1) annihilates the east-minus-west contrast across 26.5N that geostrophic transport IS, so the head clears the wind bar) or REPRESENTATION-LIMITED (the head does not clear it either, and the pentad codec has not learned transport). Inputs are #392's verbatim, all 25 - only doc changed. EVAL ONLY: --steps 60000 = the checkpoint's own step, zero training.
